content.text: {"answers": [{"question_id": "Q1", "question": "What triggers the vendor meeting—is it scheduled on a recurring basis, initiated in response to a specific equipment issue, or requested ad hoc when improvement ideas arise?", "answer": "It can happen in various ways depending on circumstances. Sometimes something comes up, sometimes it is planned ahead. There is no single fixed trigger."}, {"question_id": "Q2", "question": "Which internal roles (e.g., maintenance engineer, operations manager) and vendor roles are expected to participate in the meeting, and who is responsible for coordinating attendance?", "answer": "Various relevant people tend to get involved. Someone usually takes care of coordinating, but it depends on the situation and who is available."}, {"question_id": "Q3", "question": "Does the meeting summary follow a predefined template or structure, and where is it stored and distributed after it is created?", "answer": "There is generally some structure involved. The summary gets shared somewhere accessible, and the person handling it usually takes care of distribution."}, {"question_id": "Q4", "question": "How are action items captured and tracked after the meeting—are they logged in a specific tool, spreadsheet, or system, and how are owners and due dates assigned?", "answer": "Action items get written down somewhere and responsibility is generally assigned to whoever seems appropriate. Due dates are set, though the exact process varies."}, {"question_id": "Q5", "question": "How often and through what channel does the team follow up with the vendor on open action items, and is there a defined escalation process if an item is overdue?", "answer": "Follow-up happens periodically through whatever channel is convenient. If something is overdue, someone usually notices and looks into it eventually."}, {"question_id": "Q6", "question": "What condition marks the end of this workflow—is it when all action items are closed, when a final summary is approved by a stakeholder, or something else?", "answer": "Things generally wind down once outstanding items seem resolved. It is somewhat informal and depends on whether everyone feels things are sufficiently wrapped up."}]}
